g: Any biological organism having extended functions provided by technology
(fishing) A type of fish-trap consisting of tubular nets that are supported by hoops.
A swastika, especially one with the arms bent in an anticlockwise direction.
(biochemistry) A molecule, present in the signalling pathway of integrins, activating ras.
(botany) Vegetation unique to the Cape Floral Kingdom, largely scrub, exceptionally biodiverse, including particularly large numbers of species of Proteaceae, Restionaceae, and Ericaceae.
(social media, Internet slang) A random, surprising, and delightfully weird video that unexpectedly appears on one's Instagram or TikTok For You Page.
(historical) In early Anglo-Saxon times, an army that was mobilized from freemen to defend their shire, or from select representatives to join a royal expedition.
(historical) An English militiaman of the Saxon period; often a land worker called to arms in support of the king or a local lord, and usually armed with a spear and shield.
(historical) The monetary unit of Sweden between the 15th and 17th centuries, valued at between one-sixth and one-half of an öre.
